findings.title: Value containing backslash followed by ';' or '#' does not round-trip
findings.property: parse(stringify(obj)) deep-equals obj for string values
findings.actual: {a:'\\'} (the ';' is treated as a comment start)
findings.evidence: stringify escapes ';' and '#' with a backslash but does not escape a preceding backslash, so the output 'a=\\;' is read by parse as an escaped backslash followed by an unescaped comment marker. encode/decode are a documented inverse pair, and safe() exists to make values round-trippable.

review.title: stringify/parse does not round-trip string values with a backslash before ';' or '#'
review.reason: `unsafe()` treats `\\` as an escaped backslash, and `\;` or `\#` as an escaped comment character. `safe()` escapes only `;` and `#`, and never escapes the backslash. So the value `\;` is written as `\;`, which `unsafe()` reads as a backslash followed by an unescaped `;`. The rest of the value is dropped as a comment, so data is silently lost. The same asymmetry loses data for any value with consecutive backslashes (`\\` comes back as `\`). `safe()` and `unsafe()` are exported as a pair, and `safe()` already falls back to `JSON.stringify` for other values that would not survive, so a small fix is plausible, such as quoting values that contain a backslash next to a backslash, `;` or `#`. The input is a valid string and nothing in the code or tests excludes it. The only doubt is that the corner case is narrow and the README makes no explicit round-trip promise.

findings.title: Single-quote character value parses as empty string
findings.evidence: safe() guards its quote check with val.length > 1, so a lone "'" is emitted unquoted, but unsafe()'s isQuoted has no length check: a single quote both starts and ends with "'", so slice(1,-1) yields ''. The two halves are inconsistent.

review.title: A lone single-quote value is parsed as an empty string (stringify/parse round-trip fails)
review.reason: In lib/ini.js, safe() deliberately skips quoting when val.length > 1 is false, so "'" is written unquoted as `a='`. unsafe() then calls isQuoted("'"), which is true because the string both starts and ends with "'". The single-quote branch slices it to '', and JSON.parse('') throws and is ignored, so the value becomes ''. A lone `"` survives because JSON.parse fails and leaves it unchanged, so the single-quote path is the only broken one. The repro uses the API correctly and a one-character value is a valid string, so a length check in unsafe's quote handling would be an easy fix a maintainer would likely accept. The impact is narrow.
